analysis: This batch contains only documentation and a changelog: changelog.d/provider-fast-reconnect.md, docs/architecture/components/provider.md (new paragraph at head lines 119-143) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (runtime-constants rows near line 1968). No source code is supplied, so the actual reconnect implementation (CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, CoordinatorClientState.swift, CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift) was not reviewed here. The documented behavior is that a session open for 60s or more resets the backoff. A coordinator close frame with code 1012 gives a random 0-1s wait without growing the backoff. All other closes and failures keep the exponential backoff (base 1s, max 30s). The close code is read from the first two bytes of the close frame payload when Network.framework reports noStatusReceived. Security notes for later review: (1) A reconnect wait of 0-1s after a coordinator-sent 1012 is controlled by the coordinator, which is trusted, so there is no adversarial provider or consumer path to it. A network on-path attacker would need to break TLS to forge a close frame, so none is assumed. (2) The documentation states that registration, attestation, per-socket fresh nonce and endpoint-resumption custody proof (TB-002, TB-011, T-053) are unchanged, and that the old connection's requests are still cancelled. Faster reconnects still pass the platform authorization decision, which is outside this repo's evidence. (3) Reconnect storms or thundering herd on coordinator restart are mitigated only by the random jitter of 0-1s. That is an availability and tuning question for the platform, not a provider security regression. (4) Whether the code matches the documentation (stable-session measurement from the register frame, 1012 parsing bounds, no backoff reset on rapid flap) cannot be verified from this batch, so a code-level pass over the Swift files is advisable. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by the documentation alone.
